title: Reverse pulmonary arterial hypertension and its cardiovascular consequences

concept.text: Proposed innovation: develop treatment that durably repairs the diseased pulmonary arteries and restores right-ventricular function in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The intended capability joins recovery of the vessels carrying blood through the lungs with recovery of the right side of the heart. It would make successfully treated forms of PAH substantially reversible.

Conceptual scope: success would require sustained reversal of disease-related vascular remodeling—the structural changes in pulmonary vessels—together with meaningful recovery of right-heart performance. Lower pulmonary pressures, better exercise capacity and fewer clinical events would be important evidence, but those findings would not individually establish anatomical repair or complete cardiac recovery.

Scope proposal: pursue this capability across relevant PAH causes and disease stages while determining where recovery remains possible. The reference to possible irreversible injury identifies a boundary to investigate; it does not assume that tissue already shown to be irreversibly damaged can recover. A treatment effective in selected forms would remain a meaningful advance even if other forms required different approaches.

significance.text: Conditional significance: durable restoration of pulmonary vessels and right-heart function would change the therapeutic goal from managing the consequences of disease to recovering the affected circulation and organ function. For patients in whom this recovery occurred, substantial reversibility would follow directly from the proposed capability. This impact assessment is a reasoned consequence of the concept, rather than a finding established by the supplied scientific source.

Conditional downstream possibilities: if structural and functional recovery also translated into lasting clinical benefit, patients could experience better exercise capacity, fewer hospitalizations, less need for transplantation and longer survival. Reduced treatment burden could be another benefit, but only if studies showed that recovery could be maintained with less intensive therapy. Continued treatment might remain necessary even after substantial improvement.

Important limits: restoring pulmonary vascular function would not automatically prove reversal of advanced right-heart injury, and recovery in one PAH subtype would not establish efficacy across all causes. Likewise, a reduction in a composite clinical endpoint would not by itself demonstrate a cure. The supplied evidence cannot determine whether a universal cure exists or whether one mechanism could address every form of PAH.

missing_breakthrough.text: Proposed unsolved capability: achieve sustained repair of diseased pulmonary vessels together with recovery of right-ventricular function across a defined range of PAH causes, severity and prior treatment. The supplied materials identify this as the breakthrough target, but their accessible scientific content does not establish how much of that target remained unmet as of November 2026.

Engineering and biological barriers, framed as synthesis: treatment must produce sufficiently durable changes in vascular structure and function, and those changes must permit meaningful cardiac recovery. These are related but separate requirements. Studies would need to determine whether an apparent response reflects lasting disease modification, an effect that depends on continued treatment, or improvement in some aspects of disease while others persist.

Recovery boundaries, framed as research questions: advanced vascular remodeling and possible irreversible cardiac injury may limit what treatment can restore. A convincing development program would need to identify recoverable disease, determine how prior injury affects response, and explain differences between PAH subtypes. No supplied scientific passage resolves whether a single intervention could meet these requirements.

Measurement and safety barriers, framed as synthesis: demonstrating this capability requires connecting evidence of vascular repair with pulmonary hemodynamics, right-heart function, patient function and clinical outcomes. Researchers would also need to establish treatment duration, continued-therapy requirements, adverse effects and the durability of benefit. Improvement in one measurement cannot substitute for the full set of claims.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies sotatercept as meaningful progress and attributes a specific result to the 2025 ZENITH trial: in high-risk patients receiving background therapy, add-on sotatercept reportedly reduced a composite of death, lung transplantation or hospitalization for worsening PAH. The research further says that hospitalization largely drove the composite benefit and that the trial stopped early after a prespecified efficacy analysis. It identifies the report as Marc Humbert and colleagues, “Sotatercept in Patients with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension at High Risk for Death,” published in the New England Journal of Medicine on March 31, 2025, with DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2415160. These are attributed findings and bibliographic details from the research input; the supplied review could not verify them against scientific article content.

The evidence-access limitation is decisive for interpreting that account. According to the supplied review, the retained page contains only a cookie-access notice, with no abstract, methods or results. Although the source index records a saved, verified artifact, the review could not verify article identity from its content. Consequently, this record cannot substantiate the reported population, background treatment, composite benefit, contribution of hospitalization, early stopping or publication details through the retained scientific text. This access failure is not evidence that the reported trial result is false.

Even if the reported clinical benefit is confirmed, its relationship to this innovation requires separate assessment. Fewer deaths, transplants or hospitalizations would be clinically important, but a composite outcome alone would not demonstrate durable anatomical reversal of pulmonary vascular disease or restored right-ventricular function. Because the abstract itself was unavailable to the reviewer, the supplied evidence also cannot establish what anatomical or cardiac recovery findings the publication does or does not contain.

Temporal limitation: the supplied freshness record is empty. It establishes neither that the full breakthrough remained unachieved through November 1, 2026, nor that later work achieved it. The current evidence package therefore supports preserving sotatercept as a reported advance requiring verification, while leaving the broader state of durable PAH reversal unresolved. It supplies no verified quantitative effect size or follow-up duration to reproduce here.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: controlled studies in clearly defined PAH populations should show durable normalization or major restoration of pulmonary hemodynamics together with meaningful right-ventricular recovery. Evidence appropriate to vascular structure should accompany functional measurements if anatomical reversal is claimed. The studies should specify what constitutes major restoration and why those changes matter to patients; these are proposed requirements, not established consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Durable pulmonary hemodynamic restoration with meaningful right-ventricular recovery

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical confirmation: demonstrate improved exercise capacity and patient function, assess survival, and measure hospitalization and transplantation outcomes. Report the components of composite endpoints separately so readers can judge which outcomes account for the benefit. Functional or clinical improvement should be interpreted alongside vascular and cardiac findings rather than treated as interchangeable evidence of repair.
completion_criteria.label: Improved exercise capacity and patient function with clinical outcome reporting

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and safety assessment: follow patients long enough to distinguish sustained recovery from an early response, with follow-up duration justified in advance. Establish whether benefit requires continued therapy, what happens after clinically appropriate treatment changes, and what adverse effects or monitoring requirements accompany treatment. Continued treatment would not negate a major advance, but it would define its practical meaning.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained recovery with therapy dependence and safety established

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and breadth: seek confirmation in independent studies and across relevant causes, disease stages and background therapies, with transparent reporting of nonresponse and residual disease. Explicitly identify populations for which evidence is absent or recovery is limited. Finite trials can establish demonstrated breadth across the tested populations; they cannot prove literal universality or recovery from every degree of injury.
completion_criteria.label: Independent confirmation across tested populations with recovery limits reported

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: CAR-01, “Regenerate a severely damaged adult human heart,” overlaps through recovery of injured cardiac tissue. CAR-11 additionally requires repair of pulmonary vascular disease and evidence that the right ventricle benefits from that repair. CAR-08, “Durably reverse heart failure with preserved ejection fraction,” shares the ambition of lasting functional recovery, but its target syndrome is distinct; success in either concept would not establish success in the other.

Roster-based comparison: CAR-02, “Reliably reverse advanced atherosclerosis throughout the arterial tree,” and CAR-10, “Reverse established calcific aortic stenosis without valve replacement,” share the goal of reversing established structural cardiovascular disease. Their targets are arterial atherosclerosis and aortic-valve calcification, respectively. CAR-11 concerns pulmonary arterial disease and its right-heart consequences, so the shared ambition does not imply a shared treatment mechanism.

Roster-based comparison: CAR-03, “A durable, broadly affordable total artificial heart,” CAR-04, “A dependable supply of transplantable animal hearts,” and CAR-07, “Produce a transplantable, fully engineered living human heart,” pursue replacement of cardiac function or the heart itself. CAR-11 pursues recovery of the patient's pulmonary circulation and right heart. Reversal could conditionally reduce the need for transplantation, but cardiac replacement alone would not demonstrate repair of pulmonary vessels.

Roster-based comparison: CAR-05, “Correct inherited heart disease directly and durably in the beating heart,” overlaps with CAR-11 in the aspiration for durable treatment of an underlying disease process. Its inherited cardiac target is distinct from the range of PAH causes contemplated here. CAR-13, “Broadly prevent cardiac injury from cancer treatment without weakening cancer control,” concerns prevention during cancer therapy, whereas CAR-11 seeks reversal of established pulmonary vascular disease and cardiovascular consequences.

Roster-based comparison: CAR-06, “Make most preventable sudden cardiac deaths predictable and preventable,” CAR-09, “A durable, non-ablative cure for atrial fibrillation,” and CAR-12, “Detect actionable coronary plaque risk before a first clinical event,” address prediction and prevention, an arrhythmia cure, and coronary risk detection. These entries remain separate from CAR-11's vascular-repair and right-heart-recovery target. Its disciplinary overlap with pulmonary medicine and vascular biology does not change that distinct identity.

unresolved_issues: The retained source does not permit verification of article identity, publication details, trial population, background therapy, endpoint findings, hospitalization's contribution or early stopping.
The supplied materials do not establish the trial's quantitative effect sizes, follow-up duration, or evidence concerning anatomical vascular reversal and right-ventricular recovery.
The current extent of unmet need and any subsequent progress through November 2026 remain unassessed because the freshness record is empty.
Which PAH subtypes and disease stages permit durable vascular repair and cardiac recovery, and which require different treatments, remain unresolved.
The degree to which benefit would require continued treatment, and the boundaries imposed by irreversible injury, require evidence.
Completion thresholds, follow-up duration and acceptable treatment burdens remain proposals to be justified in a development program.

brief.title: Lasting repair of lung arteries and the right heart
possible: People with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), a disease that narrows arteries in the lungs, could regain lasting function in both those vessels and the right side of the heart. Treatment would repair the affected circulation and restore the heart’s ability to pump blood through it.
why: Restoring lung vessels and heart function would shift treatment toward recovery of the organs affected by PAH. For patients, lasting recovery could mean greater ability to exercise, fewer hospital stays, less need for a lung transplant and longer survival.

sources.who: Marc Humbert and the ZENITH Trial Investigators
sources.showed: In high-risk adults already receiving intensive treatment, adding sotatercept reduced the combined risk of death, lung transplantation or hospitalization for worsening PAH. Hospitalizations accounted for most of the difference. The trial stopped early for benefit.
sources.quote: treatment with sotatercept resulted in a lower risk of a composite of death from any cause, lung transplantation, or hospitalization (≥24 hours) for worsening pulmonary arterial hypertension than placebo.
sources.cited_for: Sotatercept improved clinical outcomes in high-risk patients.
sources.not_established: A combined clinical outcome does not establish lasting vessel repair or recovery of right-heart function.

sources.showed: An exploratory analysis conducted after the STELLAR trial found lower lung artery pressures and improvements in right-heart size and function with sotatercept. Some measures of heart performance did not improve.
sources.quote: Treatment with sotatercept for 24 weeks significantly reduced right heart size and improved right ventricle (RV) function and haemodynamic status in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).
sources.cited_for: Pressure measurements and heart imaging show progress toward recovery.
sources.not_established: These changes do not establish anatomical repair of lung arteries or lasting restoration of heart function.

sources.showed: An exploratory analysis combining PULSAR and STELLAR found better exercise capacity, lower vessel resistance and improved heart measurements. Bleeding and some blood abnormalities occurred more often with sotatercept.
sources.quote: There were clinically important reductions in both pulmonary and right heart pressures; improvements in right ventricle size during both systole and diastole; and enhancements in right ventricle contractility and right ventricular–pulmonary artery coupling.
sources.cited_for: Combined trial results connect improvements in circulation, heart function and exercise.
sources.not_established: Combining existing trials does not independently confirm lasting repair or establish benefit across every PAH subtype.

sources.showed: SOTERIA followed participants who completed earlier trials, with everyone receiving sotatercept. Walking-test distance and other benefits were largely maintained. Serious bleeding occurred.
sources.quote: Improvements in 6MWD, NT-proBNP, WHO Functional Class and SFRS achieved from baseline of SOTERIA were largely maintained at 1 year, including in the placebo-crossed group.
sources.cited_for: Follow-up supports persistence of clinical benefits during continued treatment.
sources.not_established: Selected trial completers without a comparison group cannot establish recovery without treatment or definitive long-term safety.

sources.showed: A single patient with inherited PAH showed marked recovery of right-heart pumping and clinical condition after adding sotatercept. Heart scans documented the change.
sources.quote: the administration of sotatercept over 6 months led to a complete reversal of disease progression in terms of RV function and clinical status.
sources.cited_for: A case report documents substantial heart recovery even after longstanding disease.
sources.not_established: A single patient cannot establish reproducibility, lasting vessel repair or recovery across PAH causes.

shown: Sotatercept has improved exercise capacity, lung artery pressures and measures of right-heart function in clinical trials. Humbert and colleagues also found fewer combined events of death, transplantation or hospitalization in high-risk patients.

Preston and colleagues found that clinical benefits largely persisted during continued treatment. Thal and colleagues documented marked heart recovery in a single patient with longstanding inherited PAH.
missing: Controlled evidence must connect lasting repair of lung artery structure with meaningful recovery of right-heart function.
Longer studies must establish how long recovery lasts, whether continued treatment is needed and what harms accompany it.
Independent studies must establish which PAH causes and disease stages permit recovery, and where damage remains.

milestones.label: Lasting restoration of lung circulation and right-heart function
milestones.explanation: Controlled studies would have to show lasting restoration of lung blood pressures and flow, meaningful right-heart recovery and structural evidence of claimed vessel repair. This would establish recovery of the affected circulation.

milestones.label: Better exercise and daily function with clinical outcomes reported
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to show better exercise and daily function and report survival, hospitalization and transplantation separately. This would connect vessel and heart recovery to benefits patients experience.

milestones.label: Sustained recovery with treatment needs and safety established
milestones.explanation: Follow-up would have to establish lasting recovery, continued-treatment needs, effects of appropriate treatment changes and harms. This would define how recovery can be maintained safely.

milestones.label: Independent confirmation with the limits of recovery defined
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would have to confirm recovery across tested causes, disease stages and existing treatments, while reporting nonresponse and remaining disease. This would establish who can benefit and where recovery stops.

uncertain: It remains unclear which PAH subtypes and stages allow lasting recovery, and how much advanced injury can be repaired.
Recovery may require continued treatment, and different forms of PAH may need different approaches.
The degree and duration of improvement needed to count as lasting restoration remain to be defined.

page.title: Pulmonary vascular reverse remodelling with right-heart recovery
page.definition: Treatment reverses structural disease in the native pulmonary arteries and restores right-ventricular function in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), in which narrowed lung arteries raise resistance to blood flow. Both effects persist over a prospectively specified follow-up; treatment may continue.

goal.need: Registries in economically developed countries report 48–55 adults with PAH per million. In a trial of high-risk adults on maximum tolerated therapy, 47 of 86 given placebo and 15 of 86 given add-on sotatercept died, underwent lung transplantation or spent at least 24 hours in hospital for worsening PAH. Treatment can improve the ability of lung vessels to dilate while their walls remain thickened. Lasting relief of arterial narrowing could ease the load on the right ventricle and help patients live longer.

figures.caption: ZENITH events during trial follow-up, reported on 31 March 2025
figures.note: These are observed trial proportions, not fixed-time survival estimates. Components can overlap. The trial stopped after a prespecified interim efficacy analysis.

statements.body: 7th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension, task force on risk stratification and treatment goals
statements.quote: A more attainable treatment objective is partial or complete reversal of pulmonary vascular remodelling, accompanied by regression of PH

statements.body: European Society of Cardiology and European Respiratory Society
statements.quote: Achieving and maintaining a low-risk profile on optimized medical therapy is recommended as a treatment goal in patients with PAH
statements.context: The guidelines' three-stratum model defines low risk as estimated 1-year mortality below 5%.

completion.title: A controlled human study demonstrates sustained pulmonary vascular reversal and right-heart recovery.
completion.criterion: In a defined adult PAH population, a controlled trial demonstrates regression of remodelling in native pulmonary arteries, measured directly or by a pathology-validated surrogate, together with resting mean pulmonary arterial pressure ≤20 mmHg and cardiac-MRI right-ventricular ejection fraction >54%, stroke volume index >40 mL/m² and end-systolic volume index <42 mL/m². The combined response and clinical benefit persist through prospectively specified follow-up. Continued therapy is permitted. This combination is an Atlas test; its pressure and cardiac thresholds alone do not establish vascular repair.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; an explicit composite test combining structural evidence with published haemodynamic and cardiac risk boundaries.
completion.basis: The Atlas combines evidence of arterial repair with a resting pressure boundary, three prognostic cardiac MRI cutoffs and sustained clinical benefit. A separate proposal for complete haemodynamic remission requires resting mean pulmonary arterial pressure ≤20 mmHg and cardiac index ≥2.2 L/min/m² for at least three months without treatment escalation. Arterial lesions can persist at those values. No external body specifies a minimum follow-up for the combined anatomical and right-heart response.

milestones.title: A PAH candidate improves established disease in animal experiments and is tested in two models.
milestones.criterion: Establish experimental pulmonary hypertension before treatment. Assess efficacy in two animal models using haemodynamics, right-ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary-vessel histology, and show improvement in established disease. The survey recommendations allow a response confined to one model and specify no minimum effect size.
milestones.set_by: Allan Lawrie's report of a Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute researcher survey, Summary and recommendations and Table 1; documents two-model testing practice rather than a regulatory efficacy requirement.
milestones.threshold_quote: the efficacy of any treatment should be assessed in 2 models

milestones.title: A PAH treatment reduces pulmonary vascular resistance versus placebo at 24 weeks.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized placebo-controlled trial of adults receiving background PAH therapy, meet the prespecified primary-endpoint test for a greater reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance from baseline to week 24. Resistance is mean pulmonary arterial pressure minus pulmonary arterial wedge pressure, divided by cardiac output.
milestones.set_by: Acceleron Pharma and the PULSAR investigators, registered protocol NCT03496207, primary endpoint reported in the trial publication.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary end point was the change from baseline to week 24 in pulmonary vascular resistance.

milestones.title: PAH patients gain ≥30 m walking distance and meet STELLAR's biomarker and functional-class endpoint.
milestones.criterion: At week 24, count the proportion of participants who meet all three conditions relative to baseline. Six-minute walk distance increases by ≥30 m. NT-proBNP, a marker of cardiac strain, falls by ≥30% or is maintained or achieved below 300 ng/L. WHO functional class improves or remains at class II.
milestones.set_by: Acceleron Pharma, STELLAR protocol A011-11, revision dated 6 October 2021, section 5.3; subsequently applied in an exploratory pooled analysis.

milestones.title: Treated patients meet all three ESC/ERS low-risk cardiac MRI cutoffs for right-ventricular function.
milestones.criterion: On the same follow-up cardiac MRI, right-ventricular ejection fraction exceeds 54%, stroke volume indexed to body surface area exceeds 40 mL/m² and right-ventricular end-systolic volume indexed to body surface area is below 42 mL/m². ESC/ERS assigns each value to the low-risk prognostic category. The milestone requires all three in the same patient.
milestones.set_by: ESC/ERS 2022 guidelines, Table 16, low-risk cardiac MRI column. The societies specify the individual cutoffs.

milestones.title: Add-on PAH therapy delays first death, lung transplant or ≥24-hour admission for worsening PAH.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized placebo-controlled trial of high-risk adults receiving maximum tolerated background PAH therapy, meet the prespecified superiority test for time to the first of three events: death from any cause, lung transplantation or hospitalization lasting at least 24 hours for worsening PAH.
milestones.set_by: Merck Sharp & Dohme and the ZENITH investigators, registered protocol NCT04896008, primary endpoint reported in the trial publication.
milestones.threshold_quote: death from any cause, lung transplantation, or hospitalization (≥24 hours) for worsening pulmonary arterial hypertension

milestones.title: PAH treatment benefits persist after withdrawal beyond washout of the direct vasodilator effect.
milestones.criterion: After an initial placebo-controlled benefit, keep the original placebo group on placebo and randomize participants receiving the intervention to continuation or withdrawal to placebo. Improvement in the withdrawal group must persist beyond washout of the direct vasodilator effect. Regression to the original placebo group's outcomes fails the proposed test. The task force specifies no universal washout duration or minimum effect size.
milestones.set_by: 7th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension clinical-trials task force, Figure 3; a proposed experimental test, not an adopted definition of anatomical reversal.
milestones.threshold_quote: Improvements in the outcome measures maintained beyond the washout of the direct vasodilatory effect of the intervention support a disease-modifying effect.

milestones.title: Serial intravascular ultrasound measures six-month change in pulmonary artery wall thickness.
milestones.criterion: In adults with idiopathic or systemic-sclerosis-associated PAH, measure wall thickness in matched segmental pulmonary arteries by intravascular ultrasound before treatment and at six months. Report the paired change. The registered endpoint specifies no minimum decrease and measures only the arteries accessible to the catheter.
milestones.set_by: Actelion, registered study NCT00595049, pulmonary artery wall-thickness primary outcome.
milestones.threshold_quote: Change from baseline (BL) to 6 mths in the IVUS-derived measurement of pulmonary artery wall thickness.

milestones.title: An early-treatment group retains an outcome advantage after the delayed-start group begins therapy.
milestones.criterion: Randomize participants to active treatment or placebo in a double-blind first period. In the second period, start the original placebo group on the intervention and continue treatment in the original active group. On reassessment, the delayed-start group must still fall short of the early-start group on the study outcome. The task force specifies no universal interval or numerical margin.
milestones.set_by: 7th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension clinical-trials task force, Figure 3b, proposed delayed-start design.
milestones.threshold_quote: Failure of the initial placebo group to “catch up” to the initial experimental group suggests a disease-modifying effect.

not_found: No externally adopted combined criterion or minimum duration for pulmonary vascular repair with right-ventricular recovery was found.
No qualifying randomized-withdrawal result was found for the listed PAH causes.
No controlled adult PAH study was found that demonstrated sustained native arterial repair, all specified pressure and MRI findings, and clinical benefit together.

results.finding: Sotatercept versus placebo in idiopathic PAH (n=250) was assessed for week-24 PVR change.
results.detail: The supplied text does not give a numerical effect for this subgroup or a case-specific result from PULSAR’s primary-endpoint test.

results.finding: Sotatercept versus placebo in heritable PAH (n=76) was assessed for week-24 PVR change.
results.detail: The supplied text does not give a numerical effect for this subgroup or a case-specific result from PULSAR’s primary-endpoint test.

results.finding: In drug- or toxin-associated PAH (n=17), the week-24 PVR estimate favoured sotatercept, with a confidence interval crossing zero.
results.detail: The supplied text gives the direction and uncertainty of the effect without a numerical subgroup estimate.
results.quote: the point estimate favoured sotatercept, but the confidence intervals were wide and crossed zero.

results.finding: Sotatercept versus placebo in connective tissue disease-associated PAH (n=67) was assessed for week-24 PVR change.
results.detail: The prose specifically describes uncertainty in this subgroup’s walking-distance estimate. It gives no numerical PVR result for this subgroup.

results.finding: After congenital shunt correction (n=19), the week-24 PVR estimate favoured sotatercept, with a confidence interval crossing zero.
results.detail: The supplied text gives the direction and uncertainty of the effect without a numerical subgroup estimate.
results.quote: the point estimate favoured sotatercept, but the confidence intervals were wide and crossed zero.

results.finding: In idiopathic PAH (n=250), the pooled analysis assessed time to first death or broader clinical worsening with sotatercept.
results.detail: The analysis did not test superiority on the specified three-event composite, which requires actual transplantation as one of the events.

results.finding: In heritable PAH (n=76), the pooled analysis assessed time to first death or broader clinical worsening with sotatercept.
results.detail: The analysis did not test superiority on the specified three-event composite, which requires actual transplantation as one of the events.

results.finding: Heritable PAH (n=1): pulmonary vascular resistance reached 4.9 Wood units after add-on sotatercept.
results.detail: Sotatercept was administered through a compassionate-use program.

results.finding: Heritable PAH (n=1): BNP fell to 6 pg/mL after add-on sotatercept.
Heritable PAH (n=1): right-ventricular ejection fraction reached 40.1% on follow-up cardiac MRI after sotatercept.
BMP9 normalized right-ventricular systolic pressure after 4 weeks in Bmpr2 R899X knock-in mice (11 treated, 21 untreated).
results.detail: The human disease-associated Bmpr2 knock-in supports the Heritable case. The induced rat models supply the additional efficacy tests required by m1.
results.quote: The finding that BMP9 treatment reverses established disease in three animal models of PAH is critical, as any viable treatment will need to be effective in a patient population that typically presents with advanced disease.

results.finding: In the pooled sotatercept cohort (n = 20), which included idiopathic PAH, mean six-minute walk distance increased by 57 m.
results.detail: The clinical results were pooled across the two aetiologies. The paper gives no idiopathic-specific response estimate.

results.finding: In the pooled sotatercept cohort (n = 20), which included connective tissue disease-associated PAH, mean six-minute walk distance increased by 57 m.
results.detail: The clinical results were pooled across the two aetiologies. The paper gives no connective tissue disease-specific response estimate.

results.finding: In the illustrated sotatercept-treated idiopathic PAH case (n = 1), follow-up cardiac MRI showed right-ventricular ejection fraction of 55%.
results.detail: The 18-patient pooled MRI analysis reports stroke volume and end-systolic volume in mL.

results.finding: In the illustrated sotatercept-treated systemic sclerosis-associated PAH case (n = 1), follow-up cardiac MRI showed right-ventricular ejection fraction of 55%.
results.detail: The 18-patient pooled MRI analysis reports stroke volume and end-systolic volume in mL.

results.finding: Imatinib reversed established pulmonary hypertension in 2 models, with 18 rats in the high-dose arm and 20 mice across the hypoxia arms.
results.detail: The study used induced disease models. The human tissue comparison included two idiopathic PAH cases and measured PDGFRβ expression. The treatment efficacy result comes from the animal experiments.
results.quote: We now report that the PDGF receptor antagonist STI571 (imatinib) reversed advanced pulmonary vascular disease in 2 animal models of pulmonary hypertension.

results.finding: In rats with monocrotaline/pneumonectomy PAH (n=9–11 treated, n=6–7 vehicle), inhaled seralutinib reduced right-ventricular systolic pressure by 50% versus vehicle.
results.detail: Pulmonary artery systolic pressure stayed stable during treatment in the monocrotaline model and rose in vehicle controls. The reported 50% reduction in right-ventricular systolic pressure is an endpoint comparison against vehicle.
results.quote: A 50% reduction in RVSP was observed in the seralutinib group compared to vehicle (p<0.001;  figure 4c ).

results.finding: In 8 adults with PAH, including 3 with scleroderma-associated PAH, pooled mean percent wall thickness increased by 2 percentage points at six months.
results.detail: The paper defines percent wall thickness as wall area divided by total vessel area. The 2-percentage-point change is calculated from the rounded pooled means.
results.quote: Similarly, no significant change in % wall thickness (34±2% vs 36±4%; mean±SEM, p = 0.6) was observed.

results.finding: In PAH after congenital shunt repair, the early-start 2.5 mg maximum group gained 74 m more in mean 6-minute walk distance than the delayed-start group at two years (n=19 across both groups).
results.detail: The 74 m gap is calculated from the reported means. The comparison is exploratory and uses observed cases. The trials were not designed to establish statistically significant differences in this subgroup.
results.quote:
However, the long-term response in PATENT-2 appeared to be less pronounced in patients in the former riociguat 1.5 mg–maximum or former placebo groups versus the 2.5 mg–maximum group (
figure 1
B).

results.finding: In Eisenmenger syndrome, both BREATHE-5 extension groups improved in 6-minute walking distance by week 40 (sample size unstated).
results.detail: The 53.1 m treatment effect was measured before the placebo group started bosentan. The extension narrative and figure caption describe improvement within each group without giving the between-group comparison.
results.quote:
An improvement in distance 
was achieved at week 40 in both groups.

goal.need = "Registries in economically developed countries report 48\u201355 adults with PAH per million. In a trial of high-risk adults on maximum tolerated therapy, 47 of 86 given placebo and 15 of 86 given add-on sotatercept died, underwent lung transplantation or spent at least 24 hours in hospital for worsening PAH. Treatment can improve the ability of lung vessels to dilate while their walls remain thickened. Lasting relief of arterial narrowing could ease the load on the right ventricle and help patients live longer.". Reason: The current paragraph gives trial eligibility and a symposium statement but omits the event rates patients faced and the reason arterial repair could matter to them.

edit completion: basis = "The Atlas combines evidence of arterial repair with a resting pressure boundary, three prognostic cardiac MRI cutoffs and sustained clinical benefit. A separate proposal for complete haemodynamic remission requires resting mean pulmonary arterial pressure \u226420 mmHg and cardiac index \u22652.2 L/min/m\u00b2 for at least three months without treatment escalation. Arterial lesions can persist at those values. No external body specifies a minimum follow-up for the combined anatomical and right-heart response."; refs = [2, 3, 4, 5]. Reason: The basis omits the cardiac-index and duration conditions of the published haemodynamic remission proposal, making it unclear where that proposal ends and the Atlas composite begins.
add case "Portopulmonary hypertension". Reason: The ERS identifies portal-hypertension-associated PAH as a distinct group underrepresented in randomized treatment trials.
add case "HIV-associated". Reason: The ERS identifies HIV-associated PAH as a distinct group for which additional efficacy and safety data are needed.
add case "Schistosomiasis-associated". Reason: The ERS identifies schistosomiasis-associated PAH as a distinct group underrepresented in randomized treatment trials.
add case "Eisenmenger syndrome". Reason: Eisenmenger syndrome involves reversed or bidirectional shunt flow and falls outside the existing corrected-shunt case.

edit m1: criterion = "Establish experimental pulmonary hypertension before treatment. Assess efficacy in two animal models using haemodynamics, right-ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary-vessel histology, and show improvement in established disease. The survey recommendations allow a response confined to one model and specify no minimum effect size."; threshold_quote = "the efficacy of any treatment should be assessed in 2 models"; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 7, 19]. Reason: The two-model recommendation allows responses to differ, and the dosing schedule and observed rat outcomes belong with the results.

edit m2: criterion = "In a randomized placebo-controlled trial of adults receiving background PAH therapy, meet the prespecified primary-endpoint test for a greater reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance from baseline to week 24. Resistance is mean pulmonary arterial pressure minus pulmonary arterial wedge pressure, divided by cardiac output."; threshold_quote = "The primary end point was the change from baseline to week 24 in pulmonary vascular resistance."; threshold_ref = 8; refs = [8, 3]. Reason: The current criterion mixes the prespecified resistance endpoint with PULSAR's allocation counts and observed effect size.

add milestone after m2: "Serial intravascular ultrasound measures six-month change in pulmonary artery wall thickness.". Reason: The existing human milestones omit a registered measurement of change in the arterial wall itself.

edit m3: criterion = "At week 24, count the proportion of participants who meet all three conditions relative to baseline. Six-minute walk distance increases by \u226530 m. NT-proBNP, a marker of cardiac strain, falls by \u226530% or is maintained or achieved below 300 ng/L. WHO functional class improves or remains at class II.". Reason: STELLAR defines a response within the same participant, while the pooled responder counts and subgroup sizes describe observed results.

edit m4: title = "Treated patients meet all three ESC/ERS low-risk cardiac MRI cutoffs for right-ventricular function."; criterion = "On the same follow-up cardiac MRI, right-ventricular ejection fraction exceeds 54%, stroke volume indexed to body surface area exceeds 40 mL/m\u00b2 and right-ventricular end-systolic volume indexed to body surface area is below 42 mL/m\u00b2. ESC/ERS assigns each value to the low-risk prognostic category. The milestone requires all three in the same patient."; set_by = "ESC/ERS 2022 guidelines, Table 16, low-risk cardiac MRI column. The societies specify the individual cutoffs."; threshold_quote = "RVEF >54%\nSVI >40 mL/m\u00b2\nRVESVI <42 mL/m\u00b2"; threshold_ref = 3. Reason: The title names only one of the three required MRI findings, and the guideline table supplies the missing threshold quotation.

edit m5: title = "Add-on PAH therapy delays first death, lung transplant or \u226524-hour admission for worsening PAH."; criterion = "In a randomized placebo-controlled trial of high-risk adults receiving maximum tolerated background PAH therapy, meet the prespecified superiority test for time to the first of three events: death from any cause, lung transplantation or hospitalization lasting at least 24 hours for worsening PAH."; threshold_quote = "death from any cause, lung transplantation, or hospitalization (\u226524 hours) for worsening pulmonary arterial hypertension"; threshold_ref = 1. Reason: The hazard ratio is a trial result, and the title can make clear that superiority applies to the first event in a composite.

edit m6: criterion = "After an initial placebo-controlled benefit, keep the original placebo group on placebo and randomize participants receiving the intervention to continuation or withdrawal to placebo. Improvement in the withdrawal group must persist beyond washout of the direct vasodilator effect. Regression to the original placebo group's outcomes fails the proposed test. The task force specifies no universal washout duration or minimum effect size.". Reason: The withdrawal test needs its continuing-placebo comparator, while SOTERIA's on-treatment outcomes do not define the test.

add milestone after m6: "An early-treatment group retains an outcome advantage after the delayed-start group begins therapy.". Reason: The World Symposium also proposes a delayed-start test that can assess disease modification while both groups continue treatment.
remove not found 2. Reason: The full 2026 ERS treatment update is available in the European Respiratory Journal.

add not found: "No controlled adult PAH study was found that demonstrated sustained native arterial repair, all specified pressure and MRI findings, and clinical benefit together.". Reason: The existing evidence gap concerns adoption of a test and leaves open whether a study has already met it.
